Alteration Classes for an Alteration Matrix

Source: R/figure-data-annotations.R
AlterationMatrixData.Rd

Turns a gene-by-sample table of alteration types (several types joined by a separator) into one class per gene and item: types are mapped to classes (for example nonsense, frameshift and splice variants to "Truncating"), and a gene with more than one class in a sample is "Multiple". Genes are selected and ordered as first, then genes altered in at least min_count samples by decreasing count (ties in table order), then last.

Usage

AlterationMatrixData(
  matrix,
  gene = NULL,
  ids,
  id_map = NULL,
  map_from = NULL,
  map_to = NULL,
  first = NULL,
  last = NULL,
  min_count = 1,
  classes = list(Truncating = c("Nonsense", "Frameshift", "Splice")),
  multiple = "Multiple",
  separator = "|"
)

Arguments

matrix

Data frame: gene column and one column per sample; empty or missing entries mean no alteration.

gene

Gene column (default the first column).

ids

Items (columns of the plot) in order: vector or data frame ordered by rank.

id_map

Optional data frame mapping items to sample columns.

map_from, map_to

Columns of id_map.

first, last

Genes always shown first and last.

min_count

Smallest number of altered samples for other genes.

classes

Named list: class to the types it collects; other types keep their name.

multiple

Class of genes with several classes in one sample.

separator

Separator of several types in one entry.

Value

A long data frame with gene, id, class (missing if none), count (altered samples of the gene in the table), percent (count relative to the number of items) and gene_rank.

Examples

m <- data.frame(gene = c("G1", "G2"), S1 = c("Missense", ""), S2 = c("Nonsense|Missense", "Deletion"))
AlterationMatrixData(m, ids = c("S1", "S2"), min_count = 1)
#>   gene id    class count percent gene_rank
#> 1   G1 S1 Missense     2     100         1
#> 2   G1 S2 Multiple     2     100         1
#> 3   G2 S1     <NA>     1      50         2
#> 4   G2 S2 Deletion     1      50         2
